extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, researchers, and journalists interested in media controversies and Canadian higher-education/race issues
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic Wikipedia article documenting the 2010 Maclean's 'Too Asian' controversy — its content, criticism, protests, government and institutional responses, and aftermath. The page summarizes claims, media reactions, community activism, and consequences for the magazine and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid racist or stereotypical framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The article was widely criticized for being 'racist, stereotypical and reductive', framing 'Asian' students as single-minded, socially inept hard-workers and implying a cultural trait that makes campuses 'too Asian'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not portray racial or ethnic groups as monolithic caricatures. Avoid characterizations that reduce people to stereotypes (e.g., 'single-minded', 'socially inept') or that imply collective moral/behavioral deficiencies. Provide nuance and avoid language that could be read as denigrating an identifiable group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate 'Asian' with a single ethnicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics took issue with the piece's conflation of 'Asian' with Chinese — the article quoted a number of Chinese students while failing to address that 'Asian' subsumes many different ethnic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing broad categories like 'Asian', explicitly acknowledge internal diversity and, where relevant, distinguish between specific ethnicities (e.g., Chinese, Indian, Filipino). Avoid using examples or sources from a single subgroup as if they represent the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate international versus domestic (Canadian-born) students
rubrics_metrics.description: The article made no distinction between international students and Canadian-born 'Asians' — an important distinction that was completely disregarded in the survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify respondents' status (international vs domestic) when reporting on student populations and admissions issues. Treat these populations separately when their experiences, legal statuses, or enrollment incentives differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid perpetuating model-minority or meritocracy myths
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentators argued the article inaccurately perpetuated the myth that universities functioned as meritocracies and relied on the 'model minority' framing that Asians succeed purely by merit or cultural traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about uncritically accepting or promulgating narratives (e.g., meritocracy, model-minority) that obscure structural barriers, discrimination, or differing opportunities. Provide evidence and context when discussing achievement differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify factual claims and quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Several people interviewed said they had been misquoted, or that the authors were dishonest in their explanation of opinions; Havergal College's principal stated the magazine never confirmed that named students actually attended the school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-check attendance, affiliations, and quotations. Confirm identities and claims with reliable sources. Avoid publishing statements that cannot be corroborated; correct clear errors promptly and transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly contextualize or condemn discriminatory viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece never explicitly condemned Alexandra and Rachel's belief that certain universities were 'too Asian', which critics said indirectly condoned that entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on discriminatory or prejudicial views, contextualize them within ethical and social frameworks and, where appropriate, make clear the reporter/editorial stance so as not to implicitly legitimize or normalize exclusionary beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include diverse perspectives and representative sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics argued the article's discussion of 'over-representation' and campus experience relied on limited voices and did not adequately represent the range of Asian identities or other affected stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek a balanced set of sources representing different ethnicities, students (domestic/international), faculty, administrators, and community organizations. Avoid privileging a narrow sample that could skew conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensational or offensive headlines/titles
rubrics_metrics.description: The article's title was changed twice (from 'Too Asian' to variations) and drew sharp criticism; titles framed the piece in a way that many found offensive and provocative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose headlines and titles that accurately reflect content and avoid inflammatory or demeaning language toward identifiable groups. Reconsider sensational framing that may cause harm without editorial justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize comparative policy references (e.g., US quota debates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics were shocked by the article's reference to U.S. debates about race-based quotas to 'balance' campuses without sufficient context, which seemed to normalize exclusionary measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invoking policies or debates from other jurisdictions, provide full context, explain legal and social differences, and avoid presenting extreme or contested policy options as unexamined parallels or endorsements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond responsibly and be accountable to affected communities
rubrics_metrics.description: There was widespread activism, open letters, institutional motions condemning the piece, and calls for apology; Maclean's never offered an apology and negotiations failed to yield one, which intensified criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reporting causes community harm, engage respectfully with affected groups, consider reparative actions (corrections, clarifications, apologies), and enter dialogue in good faith. Transparent corrective steps can mitigate damage and restore trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain editorial oversight regardless of author seniority
rubrics_metrics.description: One author was an intern; the controversy raised questions about editorial responsibility, staffing decisions, and whether standards were sufficiently applied to pieces by junior staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that all published pieces — including those by interns or junior writers — undergo robust editorial review for accuracy, fairness, and sensitivity. Editors must take responsibility for the publication's voice and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid homogenizing complex social categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Further criticism focused on depicting 'Asians' as a homogeneous group without attention to intra-group differences in ethnicity, background, or experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating broad social categories as uniform. Where group-level language is used, qualify it, provide breakdowns if possible, and recognize intra-group variation in experiences and perspectives.
